1.s: Luke writes an orderly account for Theophilus. The angel Gabriel announces the birth of John to old Zechariah, and of Jesus to Mary, who answers, “Let it be done to me according to your word.” Mary visits Elizabeth and sings the Magnificat; John is born.
1.d: Mary’s song, the first of three songs of praise around Jesus’ birth, is much like Hannah’s prayer in 1 Samuel 2:1–10 [[tosn:Luke 1:46-55]]; it sings of God rescuing his people [[bsn:Luke 1:39-56]]. Zechariah’s song is called the Benedictus, Latin for “Blessed” [[tosn:Luke 1:67-79]].

2.s: Jesus is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger; angels announce good news to shepherds. He is presented in the temple, where Simeon and Anna recognize him. At twelve he stays behind in his Father’s house.
2.d: Shepherds were sometimes looked down on, and Jesus came to people like them, ordinary, poor and humble [[tosn:Luke 2:8]]. Simeon’s song, the Nunc Dimittis, praises God for letting him see his salvation [[tosn:Luke 2:29-32]]: “a light for revelation to the nations” [[bible:Luke 2:32]].

3.s: John the Baptizer preaches repentance and sharing. Jesus is baptized and the Spirit descends. Luke gives Jesus’s family tree back to Adam, “the son of God”.
3.d: Luke traces Jesus’ family back to Adam, which may show that he is connected to all people [[tosn:Luke 3:23-38]] [[bsn:Luke 3:23-38]]. The fifteenth year of Tiberius may be counted from AD 11 or AD 14 [[tosn:Luke 3:1]].

4.s: Jesus is tempted in the wilderness. In the Nazareth synagogue he reads Isaiah 61, “The Spirit of the Lord is on me… to preach good news to the poor” and says, “Today this Scripture has been fulfilled.” The town tries to kill him.
4.d: In Nazareth Jesus reads Isaiah 61 and says, “Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing” [[bible:Luke 4:21]]. “The acceptable year of the Lord” [[bible:Luke 4:19]] recalls the Year of Jubilee, when debts were forgiven and slaves set free, a picture of God’s salvation [[tosn:Luke 4:18-19]]. He reminds the crowd of God’s care for the widow of Zarephath and for Naaman, both foreigners [[bible:Luke 4:25-27]].

5.s: A miraculous catch of fish; Peter says, “Depart from me, for I am a sinful man.” Jesus heals a leper and a paralysed man, calls Levi, and says he came to call sinners to repentance.
5.d: New wine stretches as it ferments and would burst old, brittle wineskins [[tosn:Luke 5:36-38]]: “new wine must be put into fresh wine skins” [[bible:Luke 5:38]].

6.s: Sabbath conflicts; Jesus chooses the Twelve after a night of prayer. The Sermon on the Plain: blessings on the poor and woes on the rich; love your enemies; build on the rock.
6.d: “Blessed are you who are poor” [[bible:Luke 6:20]]: in Luke the blessings for the poor are balanced by warnings to the rich; those who trust in themselves will be humbled, and those who depend on God will be blessed [[tosn:Luke 6:24-26]].

7.s: Jesus heals a centurion’s servant and raises a widow’s son at Nain. A sinful woman weeps on his feet and anoints them: “Her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much.”
7.d: Jesus has more friendly contact with Pharisees in Luke than in the other Gospels, as when one invites him to dinner [[tosn:Luke 7:36]]. When Jesus touches the unclean, he is not made unclean; he makes them clean [[tosn:Luke 7:13-14]].

8.s: Women who travel with and support Jesus are named. The parable of the sower. Jesus calms a storm, frees a man possessed by Legion, heals a bleeding woman and raises Jairus’s daughter.
8.d: Some of these women, like Joanna, came from wealthy families and supported Jesus’ ministry [[tosn:Luke 8:2-3]], serving “from their possessions” [[bible:Luke 8:3]]. Mary Magdalene later plays a key part at the burial and resurrection [[tosn:Luke 8:2]].

9.s: The Twelve are sent out; five thousand are fed; Peter confesses Jesus as “the Christ of God”; the transfiguration. Jesus “intently set his face to go to Jerusalem”.
9.d: From 9:51 the rest of Luke’s Gospel follows Jesus’ journey to Jerusalem and his work there [[bsn:Luke 9:51-62]]. The feeding of the crowd points ahead to God’s great feast for all nations [[tosn:Luke 9:10-17]].

10.s: Seventy (or seventy-two) are sent out. The parable of the Good Samaritan answers, “Who is my neighbor?” Martha is busy serving while Mary sits at Jesus’s feet.
10.d: A “neighbor” was normally thought of as a fellow Israelite [[tosn:Luke 10:29]], but in God’s kingdom a despised foreigner becomes the true neighbour [[tosn:Luke 10:33]]. Jesus turns the question “Who is my neighbor?” into “which of these three do you think seemed to be a neighbor” [[bible:Luke 10:29]] [[bible:Luke 10:36]].

11.s: Jesus teaches the Lord’s Prayer and urges persistent asking: “How much more will your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him!” Woes on Pharisees and lawyers.
11.d: By driving out demons Jesus was destroying Satan’s kingdom and showing that God’s kingdom was present [[tosn:Luke 11:17]] [[tosn:Luke 11:20]]: “if I by God’s finger cast out demons, then God’s Kingdom has come to you” [[bible:Luke 11:20]].

12.s: Beware of hypocrisy. The parable of the rich fool. “Consider the ravens… consider the lilies.” Be ready like servants waiting for their master.
12.d: “For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also” [[bible:Luke 12:34]]. Jesus calls his followers to store up treasure in heaven [[tosn:Luke 12:33]].

13.s: Repent, or likewise perish. Jesus heals a bent-over woman on the Sabbath. The mustard seed and yeast. The narrow door. Jesus laments over Jerusalem.
13.d: Those who died at Siloam were not worse sinners than others; Jesus calls everyone to turn to God [[bsn:Luke 13:1-9]]. His healings and his driving out of demons showed God’s kingdom already present [[tosn:Luke 13:32]]. “There are some who are last who will be first” [[bible:Luke 13:30]].

14.s: At a dinner Jesus teaches humility and inviting the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind. The parable of the great banquet; counting the cost of discipleship.
14.d: Jesus turns the social order upside down: invite those who have no status and cannot repay you [[tosn:Luke 14:12-13]]. In the parable of the great feast, the message of God’s kingdom spreads to all people [[bsn:Luke 14:15-24]].

15.s: Three parables of lost things: a lost sheep, a lost coin, and a lost son whose father runs to welcome him home, while the elder brother refuses to join the celebration.
15.d: All three stories are about God welcoming the lost [[bsn:Luke 15:1-10]] [[bsn:Luke 15:11-32]]. Like the religious leaders, the older brother will not rejoice when his brother is found [[tosn:Luke 15:28]], and the parable ends without telling us how he answered [[tosn:Luke 15:31]].

16.s: The parable of the shrewd manager, and of the rich man and Lazarus, the poor man at his gate.
16.d: “You aren’t able to serve God and Mammon” [[bible:Luke 16:13]]. God cares deeply for the poor [[bsn:Luke 16:19-31]]: the rich and proud will be brought low, and the poor and humble lifted up [[tosn:Luke 16:19-31]].

17.s: Forgive repeatedly; faith like a mustard seed. Ten lepers are healed and only one, a Samaritan, returns to give thanks. “God’s Kingdom is within you.”
17.d: The phrase translated “God’s Kingdom is within you” can also mean among you, in your midst: the kingdom was already being shown in Jesus’ words and actions [[tosn:Luke 17:20-21]] [[bible:Luke 17:21]].

18.s: The persistent widow; the Pharisee and the tax collector at prayer: “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” Jesus blesses children and heals a blind beggar near Jericho.
18.d: Believers can hold on through hard times by praying and not giving up [[tosn:Luke 18:1-8]]. Prayer is not for boasting: Jesus’ disciples should pray like the tax collector [[bsn:Luke 18:1-17]], “God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” [[bible:Luke 18:13]]

19.s: Zacchaeus, a rich tax collector, climbs a tree to see Jesus and welcomes him: “Today, salvation has come to this house.” Jesus weeps over Jerusalem and clears the temple.
19.d: “For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost” [[bible:Luke 19:10]]; many see this verse as the main theme of Luke’s Gospel [[tosn:Luke 19:1-10]].

20.s: Leaders question Jesus’s authority. The parable of the wicked tenants. Questions about taxes and the resurrection: God is “not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
20.d: The chief priests, scribes and elders, the most powerful leaders in Jerusalem, united against Jesus because he threatened their authority [[tosn:Luke 20:1]]. He warns against leaders who would take over widows’ houses [[bsn:Luke 20:45-21:4]].

21.s: A poor widow gives two small coins, more than all the rich. Jesus foretells the temple’s destruction and Jerusalem surrounded by armies.
21.d: Herod the Great had rebuilt the temple into one of the great buildings of the ancient world [[tosn:Luke 21:5]]. Jesus foretells its destruction, but makes clear that these events do not mean the end will come at once [[tosn:Luke 21:8-11]].

22.s: Judas agrees to betray Jesus. At the Last Supper Jesus says, “Do this in memory of me,” and that the greatest must serve. He prays on the Mount of Olives, sweating like drops of blood, is arrested; Peter denies him, and Jesus looks at Peter.
22.d: God confirmed his covenants with the blood of a sacrifice; Jesus’ death begins the new covenant promised in Jeremiah 31:31–34 [[tosn:Luke 22:20]]: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood” [[bible:Luke 22:20]]. At the arrest he would not fight [[bsn:Luke 22:47-62]], and he heals the servant’s ear [[bible:Luke 22:51]].

23.s: Jesus is tried before Pilate and Herod. On the cross he prays, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing,” promises a thief, “Today you will be with me in Paradise,” and dies saying, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.”
23.d: Pilate and Herod both find Jesus innocent, the righteous servant of Isaiah 53 who suffers for his people [[tosn:Luke 23:14-15]] [[tosn:Luke 23:47]]. From the cross he says, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing” [[bible:Luke 23:34]], promises the thief Paradise [[tosn:Luke 23:43]], and prays the words of Psalm 31:5 [[tosn:Luke 23:46]].

24.s: Women find the tomb empty. On the road to Emmaus the risen Jesus walks with two disciples, explains the Scriptures, and is recognized in the breaking of bread. He appears to the eleven, eats fish, and is taken up into heaven.
24.d: The early church worshipped on Sunday because Jesus rose on the first day of the week [[tosn:Luke 24:1]]. Jesus shows that the Scriptures foretold that the Christ must suffer [[tosn:Luke 24:25-26]], in all three parts of the Hebrew Bible: the Law, the Prophets and the Writings [[tosn:Luke 24:44]]. “Weren’t our hearts burning within us?” [[bible:Luke 24:32]] The story goes on in Acts [[bible:Acts 1:1-3]].
